evidence: app/app/pages/abilities/[name].vue:1 — the whole feature is one self-contained route file; delete it and the route is gone
app/app/pages/pokemon/[name].vue:89-95 — abilities data shaping in load() must be hand-excised from the Pokémon page
app/app/components/PokemonCard.vue:28 — `hidden` prop / 'Hidden ability' text exists only for the Abilities feature and would be dead code after removal
app/app/assets/css/main.css:199 — `.hidden-ability` (and `.muted` uses) would be orphaned in the shared stylesheet
removability.rationale: Routes are cleanly self-contained, but the feature leaves a prop, a data-mapping block and CSS rules behind in three shared files, which is the textbook 'handful of scattered edits'.

evidence: app/app/components/PokemonCard.vue:19 — the sprite URL is built in exactly one component used by all four card lists, so a sprite fix lands once
app/app/lib/pokeapi.ts:82-83 — an unused `spriteUrl` helper encodes the same URL pattern, a divergent duplicate of the line above

app/app/lib/pokeapi.ts:226 — `speciesCardsForRefs` sorts card lists; forked copy at app/app/pages/abilities/[name].vue:21 does the same sort, so ordering changes land twice (three counting buildIndex at pokeapi.ts:203)
app/app/pages/[...slug].vue:6-7 — the 404/status incantation is repeated identically in five files (also moves:31-32, abilities:36-37, types:45-46, pokemon:121-122)
changeability.rationale: Fetching, caching and the card component are single-place, so most fixes are obvious; but the dead sprite helper, the duplicated card-list sort and the five-fold 404 pattern mean several common changes land N times.

evidence: app/app/components/MoveTable.vue:7-13 — presentational component with a narrow, fully-typed row/column interface and no knowledge of the API
app/app/lib/pokeapi.ts:55-80 — all HTTP fetching, caching and concurrency live in one module; pages never call fetch directly
app/app/composables/useApiBase.ts:1-9 — one explicit resolver for the API origin instead of ad-hoc env reads across pages
app/app/assets/css/main.css:1-515 — one global stylesheet shared by all pages/components; class names like .badge, .result-count are known everywhere and to no single owner
app/app/pages/pokemon/[name].vue:44-108 — load() handles raw API responses with untyped `any` casts, so response-shape knowledge is smeared across page files rather than typed in lib
coupling.rationale: Server/client code is well separated and components depend on narrow interfaces; the global CSS file and pervasive `base` string threading are real but contained tangles.

evidence: app/app/components/PokemonCard.vue:5-10 — the card stretches across four list contexts with optional `types`/`hidden` props instead of variants
app/app/lib/pokeapi.ts:217-227 — `speciesCardsForRefs` is a real shared abstraction, but it could not stretch to carry the hidden flag, so app/app/pages/abilities/[name].vue:14-22 forks it
app/app/pages/moves/[name].vue:30-40 vs app/app/pages/abilities/[name].vue:35-40 — the detail-page skeleton (load + 404 + title) is copied, not abstracted; an Items page would be a fourth copy
app/app/components/MoveTable.vue:12-20 — `showLevel` boolean flag is the only flag-creep, and a justified one
abstraction_design.rationale: The variation the app actually has (card lists with per-context extras, sortable tables) is designed for, but the resource-page pattern is copy-paste rather than an abstraction, and one helper got forked instead of extended.

findings.issue: Dead `spriteUrl` helper duplicates the sprite URL pattern that is actually used inline at app/app/components/PokemonCard.vue:19; a sprite-related fix can land in the dead code and never reach the UI
findings.suggestion: Delete the helper, or use it from PokemonCard so the URL exists in exactly one place

findings.issue: Card-list construction (alternate-form filter, dedup, dex sort) is a fork of `speciesCardsForRefs` (app/app/lib/pokeapi.ts:217), duplicated only to attach the `hidden` flag
findings.suggestion: Extend the shared helper to accept a per-ref mapper so the ability page can annotate without copying the algorithm

findings.issue: The load-null / setResponseStatus / useHead-title 404 pattern is repeated verbatim in five page files, so changing not-found behaviour (or the title format) means five edits
findings.suggestion: Extract a `useResourcePage` composable, or throw `createError({ statusCode: 404 })` with a single error page (the idiomatic Nuxt seam)

findings.issue: All styles live in one 515-line global stylesheet with per-feature selectors interleaved; removing a feature orphans rules and renaming a class risks cross-page breakage
findings.suggestion: Move component styles into scoped `<style>` blocks (or per-component CSS files) so styles travel with their component

findings.issue: The API origin is threaded as a `base: string` parameter through every lib function and every page call site; adding any second environment knob means touching every signature
findings.suggestion: Bundle the base (and cache) into a single ApiClient object created once per request, passed as one argument

findings.issue: The composable writes to a `useState` value on every server invocation while appearing to be a read; a reader can't tell where the value is set
findings.suggestion: Just return `useRuntimeConfig().public.apiBaseUrl` (Nuxt's runtime config is already env-overridable and SSR-safe); drop the useState indirection

findings.issue: Page load functions shape raw API responses via untyped `any` casts; refactoring response handling relies on grep rather than the compiler
findings.suggestion: Declare interfaces for the API records (pokemon, move, version-group) alongside the existing NamedRef/LocalizedName ones in lib

findings.issue: Build artifacts sit inside app/ and the root .gitignore only excludes /data/, /.data-cache/ and node_modules/, so generated output risks being committed
findings.suggestion: Add a .gitignore in app/ covering .nuxt/ and .output/

summary: This is a tidy, current-idiom Nuxt 4 app: a real data-access layer with request-time caching, one composable for config, and presentational components with narrow props, so the highest-risk logic (fetching, caching, sprite URL, table sorting) is centralized. The editability drag is page-level copy-paste — the 404/title incantation in five files, a forked card-list builder, and a dead helper duplicating the sprite URL — plus one global stylesheet that no single feature owns. It's comfortable to work in but not yet a codebase where similar changes obviously land in one place.
